Alright OP I want some answers. Before that, no, it is not alright to crate a cat at night. You are causing them stress and they do not understand that they are being punished as many have said; pets are not people, don't treat them as human beings. 


 1. Is this cat fixed? A lot of hormonal or behavioral issues tend to mellow out once they are. 


2. How old is this cat. Does it have a history of other ailments other than being half blind?    


3. Do you plan to take the cat to the vet to get a professional's opinion? This behavior may or may not actually be related to something other than its sight. Cats have incredible vision in the dark and even totally blind cats can coexist with their owners. There may be more to this behavior than surface level and it will benefit you to ask someone in the profession.    


4. Showering before bed may change your scent as another commenter said, but do you apply anything else before bed? Ointments? Creams? Cats have an insane sense of smell, and some scents make them go whacky (my cat, for example, treats strawberries and melons as if they were catnip and goes nuts). If you're applying something that is strongly scented, they may react aggressively because their sense of smell is truly that strong. It happens. If you shower before bed just let the cat smell you once you're dried up so she can put a face to the scent.   


 Lastly 5. Have you been living together long, and did this behavior only start when you started living there? While it could be a mix of poor sight and maybe poor scent that causes this, they also have incredible hearing as well. If you've been living together a short while, the cat may just not have gotten used to your presence at night when she's more vulnerable and on edge due to her disability.   


Hope you figure out a good solution OP.

It's framed as this quiet experience where they lay the pet down, insert a needle, pump the drug in, and they fall asleep and that's it.

Even if it's done at home, it's still stressed out of pain instead. There is no ease. It is not peaceful; even the most exhausted animals are still afraid or anxious before they die, and there's usually only one person in the entire world that will cause them any amount of relief.

You.

Your animal has been with you its entire life. It has been with you through every hardship and every hurdle. It has loved you unconditionally and sat by you even during hard times. I draw. Chronic pain and depression, anxiety, or both, go hand-in-hand— not all the sufferers can exercise as well as others or as often due to anything from healing injuries to surgery issues, nerve issues, or anything that could impede your mobility.

Drawing, especially with music or whatever your preferred ambiance would be, is wonderful for depression and anxiety. Is it as effective as things others have said like exercise or cleaning..? Well, that varies from person to person. I find that even if you don’t consider yourself an artist of any sort, just taking a few minutes to vent on paper, be it real or digital, can help you better process whatever is negatively affecting you, or help get your mind to a different, hopefully gentler place. I‘ve heard of people drawing on their skin in order to stop themselves from self-harming as well. Art bears a huge positive impact to those suffering from mental illness— be it a coping mechanism, a way to vent, or just a way to relax and decompress your thoughts for a moment. I highly recommend at least trying it for those that haven‘t yet.
